onet.title: Industrial Machinery Mechanics
onet.description: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans.

task.title: Repair or maintain the operating condition of industrial production or processing machinery or equipment.
Repair or replace broken or malfunctioning components of machinery or equipment.
Clean, lubricate, or adjust parts, equipment, or machinery.
Disassemble machinery or equipment to remove parts and make repairs.
Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs.
Examine parts for defects, such as breakage or excessive wear.
Operate newly repaired machinery or equipment to verify the adequacy of repairs.
Record parts or materials used and order or requisition new parts or materials, as necessary.
Observe and test the operation of machinery or equipment to diagnose malfunctions, using voltmeters or other testing devices.
Analyze test results, machine error messages, or information obtained from operators to diagnose equipment problems.
Study blueprints or manufacturers' manuals to determine correct installation or operation of machinery.
Cut and weld metal to repair broken metal parts, fabricate new parts, or assemble new equipment.
Enter codes and instructions to program computer-controlled machinery.
Demonstrate equipment functions and features to machine operators.

activity.title: Maintain work equipment or machinery.
Repair worn, damaged, or defective mechanical parts.
Replace worn, damaged, or defective mechanical parts.
Adjust equipment to ensure optimal performance.
Clean equipment, parts, or tools to repair or maintain them in good working order.
Disassemble equipment for maintenance or repair.
Lubricate equipment to allow proper functioning.
Inspect mechanical equipment to locate damage, defects, or wear.
Reassemble equipment after repair.
Test mechanical equipment to ensure proper functioning.
Maintain repair or maintenance records.
Order materials, supplies, or equipment.
Record information about parts, materials or repair procedures.
Observe equipment in operation to detect potential problems.
Analyze test or performance data to assess equipment operation.
Cut materials according to specifications or needs.
Interpret blueprints, specifications, or diagrams to inform installation, development or operation activities.
Operate welding equipment.
Enter codes or other information into computers.
Train others in operational procedures.
Assign duties or work schedules to employees.
Plan employee work schedules.

element.name: Arm-Hand Steadiness

element.name: Reaction Time
element.description: The ability to quickly respond (with the hand, finger, or foot) to a signal (sound, light, picture) when it appears.

element.name: Multilimb Coordination
element.description: The ability to coordinate two or more limbs (for example, two arms, two legs, or one leg and one arm) while sitting, standing, or lying down. It does not involve performing the activities while the whole body is in motion.

element.name: Hearing Sensitivity
element.description: The ability to detect or tell the differences between sounds that vary in pitch and loudness.

element.name: Information Ordering

element.name: Selective Attention
element.description: The ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time without being distracted.

element.name: Visualization
element.description: The ability to imagine how something will look after it is moved around or when its parts are moved or rearranged.

element.name: Auditory Attention

element.name: Deductive Reasoning

element.name: Extent Flexibility

element.name: Static Strength

element.name: Trunk Strength

element.name: Written Comprehension

element.name: Category Flexibility

element.name: Inductive Reasoning

element.name: Oral Comprehension

element.name: Oral Expression

element.name: Perceptual Speed

The things to be compared may be presented at the same time or one after the other. This ability also includes comparing a presented object with a remembered object.

element.name: Response Orientation

element.name: Speech Recognition

element.name: Depth Perception

element.name: Far Vision

element.name: Flexibility of Closure

element.name: Fluency of Ideas

element.name: Rate Control

element.name: Speech Clarity

element.name: Speed of Closure

element.name: Wrist-Finger Speed

element.name: Gross Body Coordination

element.name: Gross Body Equilibrium

element.name: Sound Localization

element.name: Time Sharing

element.name: Visual Color Discrimination

element.name: Written Expression

element.name: Originality

element.name: Stamina

element.name: Memorization

element.name: Speed of Limb Movement

element.name: Dynamic Strength

element.name: Mathematical Reasoning

element.name: Number Facility

element.name: Spatial Orientation

trades.description: An Industrial Machinery Mechanic installs, repairs, and maintains factory machines and heavy equipment. They inspect moving parts, replace worn belts, bearings, and gears, line up motors, lubricate systems, and test machinery to find problems. Their work keeps production equipment running smoothly, helps prevent breakdowns, and makes workplaces safer and more reliable.

A Maintenance Mechanic who works on automatic equipment installs, inspects, repairs, and adjusts machines that run by themselves in factories, plants, or large buildings. They replace worn parts, lubricate moving pieces, test controls, and troubleshoot breakdowns with tools and meters. Their work keeps equipment running safely, smoothly, and with less downtime.

trades.description: A Packer Mechanic installs, adjusts, repairs, and maintains packing machines that fill, seal, label, and box products in factories or warehouses. They troubleshoot jams, replace worn parts, test controls, and keep equipment running smoothly during production. Their work helps goods get packed correctly, reduces breakdowns, and keeps production lines running safely and efficiently.
